title: Bounded KV-prefetch + deadline slicing for reranker to reduce P95 and protect headroom
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce end-to-end P95 for the reranking endpoint while preserving throughput and not increasing tail cost. This ticket implements a hybrid approach: bounded KV prefetch (per-request kv prefetch cap) + deadline-aware request slicing (timebox microbatches that guarantee progress on the hot path). The key idea is to limit speculative token prefetch and ensure we can provide partial ranked responses when a hard deadline is reached rather than blocking the entire microbatch.

Scope:
- Add a per-request KV prefetch budget configured by model profile and customer tier (default 512 tokens).
- Implement deadline-slicing which breaks long sequences into progressive microbatches with internal short timeouts (e.g., 15ms window) so we can flush partial scores upstream.
- Introduce a lightweight early-exit scorer that computes rough heuristics (cheap embedding dot products + 1-layer scorer) to provide a fallback ranking if full scoring misses deadline.
- Add telemetry for: per-request prefetch bytes, number of microbatches, early-exit invocations, and observed latency/quality delta.

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 latency for typical rerank request (avg 6 candidates, 1.5k token context) improves by >=25% on dedicated pools under baseline load.
- Early-exit fallback engaged <= 5% of requests and has median DCG@10 degradation <= 2% vs full scorer (measured on internal evaluation sets).
- No more than 3% throughput loss for dedicated pools at 75th percentile load.

Benchmarks (initial):
- Baseline (no prefetch cap, monolithic scoring): p50=90ms p95=330ms q95_DC G_at_10 = 0.915
- Prototype with bounded prefetch (512 tokens) + deadline-slicing: p50=95ms p95=245ms q95_DC G_at_10 = 0.902
Comments: This is a first-pass trade-off: latency improved significantly, small quality drop in tail quantiles. We will iterate on scoring heuristics and prefetch budgets per-model and make them tunable in Console.

Implementation notes:
- Runtime: Add a new RequestContext flag kv_prefetch_budget and a microbatch scheduler that accepts a request deadline. Use the existing lane scheduler but add an additional eviction rule that yields to deadline slices.
- KV prefetch: reuse existing async prefetch pipeline but add token budget enforcement at request admission and backpressure to the network layer.
- Early-exit scorer: lightweight Go service co-located on the scorer workers to avoid extra hop; initial model is a distilled MLP (100k params) that uses cached embeddings when available.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Early-exit might bias results for certain query types. Mitigation: add a per-customer opt-out flag and a shadow-mode evaluation where early-exit runs but results are discarded and logged for analysis.
- Risk: Too-aggressive prefetch cap increases downstream compute jitter. Mitigation: profile per-model token distribution and expose recommended caps in Optimize UI.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Finish microbatch scheduler PR and land basic unit tests (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/1287).
2) Wire telemetry in tracing and add dashboard (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RER/Deadline+Slicing+Design).
3) Run 72-hour canary on dedicated-staging and collect DCG/latency tradeoffs.

Notes on rollout: default enabled on dedicated pools as opt-in per-project, behind a feature flag for hosted tier for initial 2-week canary. Plan to expose prefetch_budget and deadline_window in Console under model advanced settings.
